title: Read Borrows (&)
story: Instead of giving away your book, you let someone READ it while you still own it. `&` creates a read-only reference — you keep ownership, they get access.
why: Read borrows let multiple parts of your program inspect the same data simultaneously without copying, transferring ownership, or risking data races.
analogy: & is like letting someone look at your book — they can read it, but they can't write in it, and you still own it.
try_it: Create three separate read borrows of the same Vec and pass each to a different function. All three work simultaneously.
tips: Use & when your function only needs to read, not modify
Multiple & borrows can exist at the same time — reading is safe for everyone
A read borrow prevents the owner from modifying until the borrow ends
Prefer & over cloning — borrows are zero-cost
common_mistakes: Forgetting the & when passing to a function that expects a borrow
Trying to modify through a & reference — it's read-only
Holding a & borrow while trying to move the original value
